result_text:
I changed the standard scoping rules so dotfiles and dotted folders are analysed, and only version-control metadata is ignored. The codeanalyzer test suite passes (340 run, 0 failures, 3 pre-existing skips), including a new test for the rules.

All changes are in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **Ignore rule:** the "Hidden files and folders" rule is replaced by `(.*/)?[.](git|svn|hg|bzr)/.*` (now noted "Version control metadata"). The `(.*/)?` prefix lets it match a path that starts directly with `.git/`.
- **Build and deployment:** a new rule classifies `.idea`, `.vscode`, `.vs`, `.gradle`, `.mvn`, `.settings`, `.metadata` and `.circleci` contents at any depth as build-and-deployment.
- **Dependencies:** the `.*/dependencies/.*` ignore rule is removed.

The `.yarn`, `node_modules`, `vendor` and other ignore rules are untouched.

I also added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It reads the private convention lists by reflection, since they have no getter. It checks the version-control, dotfile, IDE/build-folder and `dependencies` cases.

Nothing is committed.
